concerns.text: The success criterion SC‑001 defines project success as detecting an effect (Cohen’s d ≥ 0.3 with p < 0.05 in ≥ 80 % of bootstrap resamples). This makes the hypothesis test itself a prerequisite for project success, violating the Constitution’s Null Result Rigor principle and introducing a circular bias: a null result would be treated as project failure rather than a valid scientific outcome.

Similarly, SC‑002 requires all strata to have p < 0.05 and a coefficient‑of‑variation < 0.1. This again ties project success to achieving statistical significance across all tests, which biases the study toward confirming the hypothesis and undermines the ability to report a robust null finding.
